title: Invertibility of the fixed affine algebra homology comparison
statement: For $f,P,R,a,I,n$ as in [def-sc-affine-algebra-counit-homology-comparison], assume $I$ is K-injective and every $H^j(I)$ is quasi-coherent. Then the fixed morphism $m_{I,n}:H^n(RI)\to R(H^n(I))$ is an isomorphism. This is invertibility of a specified morphism, not mere existence of an isomorphism between these objects.

proof.text: On affine inverse images, apply higher direct image vanishing and the natural unbounded quasi-coherent pushforward comparison, justified by the bound-one truncation argument. The edge map sends cycles to cohomology classes and is invertible, with the direct-image algebra action.

For tensor pullback, adjunction of the termwise multiplication counit identifies its homology mate with this canonical edge map. Transport along the unique adjunction-compatible isomorphism from any exact P to tensor pullback. Compatibility of kernels and cokernels with that isomorphism identifies the same mate; conclude invertibility.

theorem affineAlgebraCounitHomologyComparison_isIso
    {X Y : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    (P : SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings (directImageAlgebraSpace f)) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    [P.Additive] [Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits P] [Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits P]
    (a : P ⊣ RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage (toDirectImageAlgebraSpace f))
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (I.homology n).IsQuasicoherent) (n : ℤ) :
    IsIso (affineAlgebraCounitHomologyComparison f P a I n)
